name: The Man at the Pool of Bethesda
title: The Cripple Who Was Healed
summary: A man who had been sick for 38 years lay by the Pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, hoping to be healed. Jesus healed him on the Sabbath, which led to conflict with the religious leaders. His story illustrates Jesus' power over sickness and his authority over Sabbath laws.

keyEvents.title: 38 Years Sick at the Pool of Bethesda
keyEvents.description: The man had been sick for 38 years and lay by the pool of Bethesda, which had five covered walkways. He waited for the water to be stirred so he could be healed.

keyEvents.title: Jesus Asks If He Wants to Be Made Well
keyEvents.description: Jesus saw the man lying there and knew he had been sick for a long time. He asked the man, 'Do you want to get well?' The man explained that he had no one to help him into the pool when the water was stirred.

keyEvents.title: Healed by Jesus on the Sabbath
keyEvents.description: Jesus said to him, 'Get up, pick up your mat and walk!' Immediately the man was made well, picked up his mat, and walked. This happened on a Sabbath.

keyEvents.title: Confronted by the Jews
keyEvents.description: The Jewish leaders confronted the man because he carried his mat on the Sabbath. He defended himself by saying that the one who healed him had told him to pick up his mat and walk.

keyEvents.title: Meets Jesus in the Temple
keyEvents.description: Later, Jesus found the man in the temple and said to him, 'Now you are made well. Do not sin anymore, so that nothing worse happens to you.'

keyEvents.title: Tells the Jews about Jesus
keyEvents.description: The man went and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had made him well. This led them to begin persecuting Jesus.
